messages.text: Not sure

No problem — I'll run it at 12¢ a kWh, the rough US average, and we can adjust once you check a bill.

Is this your first miner, or adding to something you already run?
how does this compare to the magic miner
Read the magic miner 40t page
Read the bsb b30 dual page
Ran the power-cost calculator · 12¢/kWh
Searched the catalog · Harlo H15 Dual Bitcoin Dogecoin
Ran the power-cost calculator · 12¢/kWh

Different jobs. The H15 Dual is $999 for 15 TH/s Bitcoin plus a Dogecoin/Litecoin chip, ~500 W — about $43/month at 12¢. The Magic Miner 40T is $799 for 40 TH/s of Bitcoin only, 650 W, about $56/month.

So the 40T gives you nearly triple the Bitcoin hashrate for $200 less — best value per TH we sell. The H15's edge is Doge.

Do you care about mining Dogecoin, or is this a Bitcoin thing?
whatever will make $

At home power the sats usually come to less than the electricity — that's not why people buy it.

What you're buying is a draw for a full block, 3.125 BTC, every ten minutes for years, plus steady sats to your own wallet and a real piece of the network on your desk. For that, the Magic Miner 40T at $799 is the one: most hashrate per dollar we sell, ships November 21, 2026.

Want me to set it up?
in a bull market, don't you think it's worth mining other coins

Fair point, and the scrypt side does pay in both Doge and Litecoin at once — they're merge-mined, so one machine, two coins.

I won't predict a market for you. But if you want a foot in both camps, the H15 Dual is the only unit that does Bitcoin and Doge in one box: $999, ships November 14, 2026. The trade is 15 TH/s of Bitcoin instead of 40.

Bitcoin-heavy or spread across both?
any other minor that you sell can mine more than 2 coins

Yes — the scrypt units. The Hammer DC06 page lists Litecoin, Dogecoin, Luckycoin, Bells, PepeCoin, Junkcoin, DingoCoin, Catcoin, DigiByte, GoldCoin and Auroracoin. Same chip, you just point it at whichever chain you like.

DC06 is 330 MH/s at about 105 W, $379.99. DC04 is 230 MH/s, $299.

None of those mine Bitcoin, though. Pair one with the 40T and you cover both sides.
do you have any video reviews on the h15?

Nothing I can point you to — the H15 page has photos only, and it's new enough that I don't want to send you a video I haven't verified is the same unit.

I've asked the team for whatever footage exists; Georges will pick it up right here and confirm by email, usually within a business day.

Anything specific you'd want to see in it — noise, setup, the Doge side?
Handed to the team · No confirmed video review or footage of the H15 Dual to link; won't send an unve
Team's been pinged — one of them will jump into this chat. If you step away, you'll get it by email.
set up and noise are the main questions

Setup is plug-and-play: built-in power supply, power cord in the box, join it to 2.4 GHz WiFi or ethernet, then enter your pool URL, worker and wallet in Harlo OS from a browser. Ten minutes, no command line.

Noise is listed at ~50 dB, fan plus heatsink. That's fridge-level — fine in an office or garage, noticeable in a bedroom at night. Honest note: the first Harlo sample was loud and they fixed it on the second.

Where would it be running?
in my wife's office downstairs where it's the coolest temps

Worth knowing: 500 W is 500 W of heat, like a small space heater running all day, and 50 dB is constant. If your wife's in that room working, she'll hear it and feel it. The 40T is more of both at 650 W.

If the room's occupied all day, the Thor P2 is the quiet one — ~40 dB, 166 W, 10 TH/s for $369.

Is she in there full time, or is it a spare room?
she is down there most of the day and using a space heater when the temps drop down below 65F

Then the heat isn't a cost, it's the point. A space heater pulls 750 to 1500 W and gives you nothing back. The 40T pulls 650 W, warms that room just the same, and hashes Bitcoin while it does it. You'd likely run the heater less.

Only real question left is the noise — 50 dB, steady fan hum, no whine. Some people find it easier to work next to than silence.

Want me to build the 40T at $799?
does the h15 have speed adjustments like the 40T

Not that I can confirm. The 40T publishes three modes — 30 TH at 450 W, 40 TH at 650 W, 50 TH at 850 W. The H15 page lists one figure, ~500 W, with no tuning range, so I won't claim it has one.

I've added it to what the team's already looking at for you, so you'll get a straight answer on that with the video.

For that office, tunable matters — you can drop the 40T to 450 W on warm days.
Ok...thanks for your responses.  I'll wait to hear from your team.  Here's my email (email hidden)
Used the chat-interview skill

Got it — noted for the team's reply.

Before you go, one thing: what's making it hard to choose between the H15 and the 40T?
I see benefits for both at this point, but this would be my first miner.  So, just want to do my due diligence and research

Makes sense for a first one.

What would you need to see to feel sure — the noise in a real room, or proof the numbers hold up?
My wife has a sensitivity to noise, but both are important to me

That changes things. If she's noise-sensitive, I wouldn't put a 50 dB unit in the room she works in all day — the 40T or H15 belongs somewhere else in the basement. The T. P2 at ~40 dB and 166 W is the one that can sit beside her.

I'll make sure the team covers noise properly when they come back to you.
Ok...thx
Thanks for talking it through — good questions for a first miner. The team will come back to you on the video and the H15 tuning.
Cool....last question, have any of your miners scored a block over all the years that you've been selling them?

Not one I can confirm, and I won't claim one I haven't seen verified. Solo blocks do get found by home miners on the Bitcoin side, but I'd want the team to tell you if any of ours has.

I've added that to what they're coming back to you with.
Sounds good...thanks and enjoy your day
You too. The team will be in touch — and if you want the numbers rerun once you check your power bill, just come back here.
Ok
Take care.
Cheers
Cheers.
